A decade ago, the crown prince led the kingdom into a war aimed at ousting the Houthis from power. The conflict turned into a quagmire for Saudi Arabia, sapping its resources and sparking widespread backlash due to its devastating bombing campaign. items.summary: Trump rules out new attack on Iran until after midterms as oil prices spike US President Donald Trump on Thursday ruled out new attacks on Iran until after the November mid-term elections, following several reports that Washington is gearing up for a new round of escalation. "We are having productive discussions with the Islamic Republic of Iran," Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social. "We will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections to be held in the United States on November 3rd.” Trump’s statement came after several news sites, including Axios, which is seen as close to Trump and his aides, reported that the Pentagon was preparing for a resumption of high-intensity strikes on Iran. The Atlantic also reported Trump is weighing attacking Iran before the US midterm elections. Read more: Trump rules out new attack on Iran until after midterms as oil prices spike

Military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group launched several operations against the airport, “resulting in the disruption of air traffic at the airport and its complete closure”. He also named King Fahd Airport in Dammam, an Aramco-affiliated petrol station and a refinery in Saudi Arabia’s Eastern Region as targets. The Riyadh strike caused the highest death toll from an attack on a Gulf country since the US-Israeli war on Iran began on 28 February. King Khalid Airport remained closed on Sunday.

items.summary: IEA confirms release of 330 million barrels of oil reserves amid Iran war disruptions The International Energy Agency (IEA) confirmed on Thursday the release of about 330 million barrels of emergency reserves of oil as part of a March agreement under which member countries agreed to release 400 million barrels to address the disruption to supplies amid the US-Israeli war on Iran. This follows IEA executive director Fatih Birol saying that about 325 million barrels had already been released under the agreement earlier this month.

clusters.headline: Delegations from over ten countries walk out of Israeli president's CICA summit speech

items.title: Delegations from over ten countries walk out of Israeli president's CICA summit speech
items.summary: Delegations from over ten countries walk out of Israeli president's CICA summit speech Representatives from more than 10 countries, including Turkey, walked out of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA) summit in Azerbaijan as Israeli President Isaac Herzog began his speech on Thursday. Iran’s deputy legal affairs minister called for Israel to be expelled from CICA following Herzog's speech in Baku. Kazem Gharibabadi was quoted as saying by Iran's IRIB news that “sustainable security” in Asia was not achieved through “threats and pressure, but through mutual respect, trust-building and equal cooperation among independent states”. “If the international community does not stop America and Israel today, their aggression will spread to all independent countries. The most important source of insecurity and instability in Asia, especially in West Asia, is the Zionist (Israeli) regime; it is time for this regime to be expelled from the CICA mechanism,” he warned.

items.title: Chinese refiners rush to buy Middle East crude as stocks fall, Kpler says
items.summary: Chinese refiners rush to buy Middle East crude as stocks fall, Kpler says Chinese refiners are stepping up purchases of Middle Eastern crude as record inventory drawdowns and a recovery in refinery activity boost demand for prompt cargoes, according to analytics firm Kpler. Chinese buyers have secured at least 80 million barrels of Saudi crude since mid-September, Kpler said on X. China’s onshore crude inventories fell by about 1.6 million barrels per day in September, the fastest pace on record. Refinery throughput is projected to reach 14.2 million barrels per day by December, adding to pressure on refiners to rebuild stocks. At the same time, Chinese refiners need to replace roughly 1 million barrels per day of Iranian supply, with the US blockade still in place, according to Kpler. Stronger Chinese demand could limit further weakness in Dubai crude pricing, particularly as escalating regional tensions continue to threaten supply flows.

Het kleine containerschip GFS Pride dat onder Singaporese vlag voer, zonk toen het gisteren tijdens de doorvaart door de zeestraat werd geraakt. Op het schip brak brand uit, meldt de maritieme dienst van Singapore. Niemand raakte gewond, de 21 bemanningsleden zijn geëvacueerd. Het tweede schip Cape Dao, dat onder de vlag van Antigua en Barbuda voer, zonk in de buurt van Oman. Dat schip werd al op 23 september door een projectiel geraakt. Een bemanningslid kwam toen om het leven. De andere opvarenden werden volgens maritieme bronnen direct na de inslag geëvacueerd. De Iraanse staatstelevisie heeft beelden getoond van beide schepen: Dat schepen zinken na een aanval in de zeestraat is zeldzaam. items.summary: Pakistan president urges Iran, US to honour Islamabad MoU Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari has urged the US and Iran to exercise restraint and honour their commitments under the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding. The MoU is a 14-point interim peace agreement signed electronically on 17-18 June between the United States and Iran, with Pakistan acting as the primary mediator. Zardari called for differences to be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy, emphasising the importance of safe maritime navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, according to a statement from his office. His remarks came during a meeting with Russian Interior Minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev in Islamabad. Zardari warned that the conflict posed serious challenges to regional stability, global energy security, trade and supply chains, stressing the need to respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all states. Kolokoltsev is on a four-day official visit to Pakistan, the first by a Russian interior minister to the South Asian country.

items.summary: Attacks on Hormuz shipping at wartime high, report says Iranian missile and drone attacks on ships in and around the Strait of Hormuz were at their most intense in the two weeks to 11 October, the highest level since the US-Israeli strikes began seven months ago, the Financial Times reported. The next most intense period of attacks was during the first two weeks of March, when 13 ships were hit, the newspaper said, citing data from naval agency UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), which monitors marine security in the region. Shipowners are reconsider carrying cargoes in the region, the report said. Six vessels were attacked on Sunday alone, making it the deadliest day of attacks on shipping near the strait since the start of the conflict, FT calculated. It added that oil shipments through Hormuz fell to just 2.9 million barrels on 11 October, the lowest daily volume this month, according to Kpler.

items.title: 'Major wipeout' of 2006 proportions could force a new GOP reckoning
items.summary: Republicans could be looking at a major wipeout in the midterm elections. Their tiny House majority was always going to be difficult to maintain, but the Senate should not be in play at all. Yet it surely is, with Democrats leading in nearly all the toss-up races , including in the reddest states, and competitive in at least a dozen of the contests that will determine which party controls the upper chamber. The Iran war is a big reason this has come to pass. It has demoralized the least indefatigably partisan part of President Donald Trump’s coalition by abandoning his promise to avoid new forever wars in the Middle East. The conflict has not only distracted from the affordability focus that many voters were expecting when they threw out the Democrats in 2024, but also directly cuts against it by spiking energy prices and increasing inflation overall at a time when it might have otherwise continued to come down. Ook de VS en andere bondgenoten hebben de aanvallen van Iran veroordeeld en zeggen op te treden tegen iedereen die namens Teheran handelt. items.title: Iran’s security chief accuses Trump administration of oil smuggling near Oman
items.summary: Iran’s security chief accuses Trump administration of oil smuggling near Oman Mohsen Rezaei has accused the Trump administration of recruiting “thugs” to smuggle oil through coastal waters off Oman. Iran’s Supreme National Security Council secretary said the UAE military and the commander of US Central Command also participate in the operation, according to state-linked news agency ISNA. Trump “claims every day that the Strait of Hormuz is open, but in response I say: ‘You are smuggling, but the strait is under Iranian control and we manage it,'” Rezaei said. He said the operation relies on a handful of “small vessels to transfer oil to larger tankers”, adding that Iran attacks them “every night”.

items.title: Iran security chief accuses Trump of ‘smuggling’ oil through Hormuz
items.summary: Iran security chief accuses Trump of ‘smuggling’ oil through Hormuz Iran’s security chief claimed on Sunday that US President Donald Trump's adminitation hired “thugs” in the coastal waters of Oman to smuggle oil through the Iranian blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. Trump “claims every day that the Strait of Hormuz is open, but in response I say: ‘You are smuggling, but the strait is under Iranian control and we manage it,'” Supreme National Security Council Secretary Mohsen Rezaei was quoted as saying by Iran's ISNA news agency. Rezaei said that the smuggling operation involves the UAE military and the commander of US Central Command (Centcom) using a handful of “small vessels to transfer oil to larger tankers” and that Iran targets them “every night”.

items.summary: Een vrachtschip is stuurloos geraakt in de Golf van Oman na een Amerikaanse aanval. Het schip was volgens de Amerikanen daarvoor vertrokken uit Iran en hield zich niet aan de Amerikaanse blokkade die voor schepen uit Iran is ingesteld. "Een Amerikaans gevechtsvliegtuig heeft met een precisiewapen de achterkant van het onder Panamese vlag varende schip Ocean Molica geraakt. Daardoor kon het schip niet meer op eigen kracht varen. De bemanning bleef ongedeerd", meldde het Amerikaanse Central Command, dat verantwoordelijk is voor het Amerikaanse leger in het Midden-Oosten, Centraal-Azië en delen van Zuid-Azië. De verklaring van de Amerikanen is vrijwel niet te checken. Persbureau Reuters heeft geprobeerd in contact te komen met de eigenaar van het schip, maar slaagde daar niet in. Hoe het met de bemanning gaat, is niet duidelijk. Feit is dat het schip zijn AIS-baken, waarmee het altijd te volgen is en dat in principe altijd aan moet staan, had uitgezet. Republikeinse kandidaten vrezen dat zij de rekening moeten betalen. Op het warme asfalt van een grote truckstop in de staat Virginia gaat het werkelijk nergens anders over. "Iedereen klaagt en het gaat er elke dag weer opnieuw over", zegt vrachtwagenchauffeur John. Hij is vandaag onderweg met een flinke lading verwerkte kip. John is net als veel andere truckers zelfstandig ondernemer. Hij voelt de pijn daarom direct in zijn portemonnee. Om geld te besparen tankt hij liever in een andere staat, waar de prijzen iets lager zijn. "Ik heb gisteren al in Georgia getankt, omdat brandstof daar goedkoper is. Daar betaalde ik zo'n 5,59 dollar per gallon (ruim 3,7 liter). Hier is het een dollar meer." "De brandstofkosten vreten mijn winst op", verzucht hij. items.summary: Gisteren maakte de Amerikaanse president Trump bekend dat Rusland per direct 300.000 ton diesel gaat leveren aan de VS. Veel is nog vaag over de afspraak. Zo is onduidelijk wanneer de diesel precies naar de VS gaat en wat het betekent voor de prijs die Amerikanen betalen aan de pomp. Op een later moment zou Rusland nog eens grotere hoeveelheden leveren, die oplopen van 500.000 tot 3 miljoen ton. Na het nieuws daalde de future price voor diesel licht. Wat het voor de prijs op de langere termijn betekent, is nog volstrekt onduidelijk. In vier vragen leggen we uit waarom de Amerikanen juist nu deze deal sluiten en wat het betekent voor Oekraïne. Waarom is deze deal nu gesloten? Trump zei het in zijn bericht waarin hij de deal aankondigde al: het gaat hem om "lagere brandstofprijzen voor Amerikanen". items.summary: Trump says Iran is ‘failing badly’ as conflict in Yemen widens US President Donald Trump on Friday left open the possibility of further military action against Iran as fighting intensifies in Yemen and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia have led to a renewed offensive. Asked why possible US military action against Iran might be delayed until after the 3 November midterm elections rather than carried out immediately, Trump told reporters: “Well, we may. I think we’ll see, but I think that, uh, they’re failing badly. Their country is failing badly." "The military is defeated. They have no navy, they have no air force. Uh, they have 300 percent inflation and, uh, Iran is in very bad shape.” The remarks, recorded in a transcript of Trump’s 9 October press briefing, did not include a specific timeline or details of what action Washington might take. The US and Israel launched their war against Iran on 28 February. items.summary: Israeli politician says assassinating Ali Khamenei was a ‘mistake’ The leader of Israel’s Democrats party on Saturday has called the assassination of Iranian Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei a “mistake”. “I think, unequivocally, the elimination of Khamenei, the father, was a mistake - not because he didn’t deserve to die, only because it doesn’t serve the interests of the State of Israel,” Yair Golan said. He also added that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s goal of toppling the Iranian government was “unrealistic”. Khamenei was assassinated at the beginning of the US-Israel war and has been succeeded by his son, Mojtaba. The new supreme leader is believed to be far less risk-averse than his father, who had issued a fatwa in 2003 banning nuclear weapons in Iran. Supporters march with portraits of Iran's slain Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei in Baghdad on 30 September 2026 (Ahmad Al-Rubaye/AFP)

items.summary: Yousof Azizi: The Iranian-American scholar pressured by the FBI to return to Iran Monday 13 April started as a normal day for Yousof Azizi, a PhD student at Virginia Tech University in America. In the morning, he took his 12-year-old daughter and four-year-old son to their schools in Baltimore, Maryland, before returning home. A vocal opponent of the war on Iran, he had been living in the US for nearly 13 years and was recognised as a prominent political commentator on Persian-language media platforms and on his YouTube channel, which has more than 68,000 subscribers. Azizi had also been involved in discussions with Congress in relation to the Iran nuclear deal during Barack Obama’s presidency. When he arrived back home that April morning, a number of FBI vehicles were parked outside his residence. Upon exiting his car, Azizi found himself surrounded by US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents, their rifles pointing straight at him. clusters.headline: Increased vessel attacks drive Hormuz oil exports 'sharply lower', report says

items.title: Increased vessel attacks drive Hormuz oil exports 'sharply lower', report says
items.summary: Increased vessel attacks drive Hormuz oil exports 'sharply lower', report says Hormuz oil exports were “sharply lower,” falling to a seven-day average of 9.9 million barrels per day as of October 7, 42 percent below prewar levels and down from about 15.5 million in September, according to Kpler data cited by the Financial Times. Kpler said that flows had recovered to prewar levels in September but "intensified attacks on vessels" had driven exports "sharply lower" this week. Energy analyst Rory Johnston also said that the latest estimate puts Hormuz seven-day average oil flow peaking at 16.2 mbpd on September 24. "Then Iran really picked up its shipping attacks and that flow unsurprisingly pulled back by 3-4 mbpd," he wrote on X. "Now seeing flow at 12-13 mbpd over the past two weeks."

items.summary: It’s been a week of vigils, protests and political upheaval – from Israel, where three years after the Hamas-led attacks, former hostages and mourners called for accountability over the failures of October 7th, as questions grow over the stalled path to peace in Gaza; to France, where mass demonstrations over chronic underfunding and poor conditions have drawn students, unions and hundreds of thousands of protesters into the streets, just months ahead of a presidential election. In Spain, Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has made the housing crisis the centrepiece of a high-stakes electoral gamble, as protests intensify following the death of a pensioner whose eviction helped ignite the movement. And in the UK, questions remain over a suspected Iranian plot targeting US aircraft at RAF Fairford, after American B-1 bombers were hastily withdrawn amid warnings of a serious and immediate threat.

items.summary: The Bunker appears originally at the Project on Government Oversight and is republished here with permission. They found no weapons of mass destruction , which was the battering ram President George W. Bush and his combative coterie used to scaremonger the U.S to invade in 2003. clusters.headline: Not since 9/11 has the UK faced such a security crisis – and threat to our liberal principles | Gaby Hinsliff

items.title: Not since 9/11 has the UK faced such a security crisis – and threat to our liberal principles | Gaby Hinsliff
items.summary: The combination of Iranian, Russian and Chinese aggression is deeply worrying: just how much more concerned about security should the country be? The first time the window-rattling roar of a B-1 bomber woke me up this summer, I thought for one crazed second we were under attack. By the second time, I’d learned to recognise the sound of US planes taking off from their base at RAF Fairford for what it was: a reminder that although Britain wants no part in this war with Iran, we cannot quite escape the consequences. We’ll feel them at the petrol pump , or in the supermarket this autumn, or in this winter’s heating bills . But living under the flight path adds an extra edge to it. The skies finally fell silent last week, but only because the bombers have been hastily summoned home after an alleged terrorist plot to attack Fairford, in which (according to the prime minister) there are “ strong indications that Iran played a part ”. If Fairford is now a target of war, did that threat disappear when the Americans did? Nobody knows. Gaby Hinsliff is a Guardian columnist Do you have an opinio

Aanvallen Afgelopen week werden de meeste tankers aangevallen sinds het begin van de oorlog tegen Iran, meldt het Maritiem Informatiecentrum (JMIC), dat onder leiding van de VS staat. Daarbij zijn ook pogingen tot aanvallen meegenomen; net als intimidatie met bijvoorbeeld overvliegende drones. De Amerikaanse president zal de vredesprijs namelijk niet krijgen, is de verwachting. Vorig jaar riep president Trump zichzelf tot rechtmatige winnaar uit. De Nobelprijs werd echter uitgereikt aan de Venezolaanse oppositieleider María Corina Machado voor "haar onvermoeibare inzet voor het bevorderen van democratische rechten voor de bevolking van Venezuela". Het Witte Huis bekritiseerde het Nobelcomité omdat het "politiek boven vrede" zou hebben laten gaan. Trump beweerde dat hij "acht oorlogen" had beëindigd en dat daarom alleen hij de prijs verdiende. items.summary: In September, as the media focused its attention on the conflict in the Strait of Hormuz and the debates at the U.N. General Assembly, some internal developments in Iran went all but unnoticed. On September 28, 32 Iranian conservatives published an open letter calling for Iran to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) as a matter of urgency. Since the “ snapback ” of U.N. sanctions on Iran in September 2025, ultraconservative Iranian lawmakers have regularly pushed for pulling out of the NPT, under which the vast majority of states have committed to not develop nuclear weapons. The Majles — Iran’s parliament — drafted a law that would have initiated the move in 2025, but it has yet to move forward. In September, some lawmakers submitted new “triple-urgency” legislation to the Majles ’ president, Mohammad Baqer Ghalibaf, who is also currently Iran’s chief negotiator These continuous calls by ultraconservatives to withdraw from the NPT have yet to produce an actual withdrawal because of a lack of political consensus. items.summary: Last week, after nearly two decades of fighting, the U.S. finally pulled the plug on its seemingly endless war in Iraq. Like our exit from Afghanistan just a few years ago, the end of fighting in Iraq was met with an eerie quiet. It doesn’t take much to figure out why so little attention is paid to the end of these wars: they mark yet another loss for America and the people in Washington who insist our military power can solve every problem, everywhere. Both conflicts are examples of American hubris — strategically incoherent wars fought with American lives at the expense of too many Iraqis and Afghans lives. But, of course, we refuse to learn our lesson. In practice, each is an excludable asset held by an identifiable actor, and the Iran war has demonstrated that they can be withheld and monetised. Kuwait will buy an estimated $400m worth of repair services and parts for Patriot air-defence systems it operates, the State Department said in a statement on Friday. The State Department also approved Egypt’s purchase of more than 2,000 FGM-148 Javelin anti-tank missiles and up to 200 Javelin launch units. The sale will come with support equipment including simulation rounds, spare parts, and US government technical assistance. The sale is estimated to cost $832m. clusters.headline: The Guardian view on the US midterms: the cost of living is on the ballot, but this is about democracy too | Editorial

items.title: The Guardian view on the US midterms: the cost of living is on the ballot, but this is about democracy too | Editorial
items.summary: Donald Trump’s unpopularity and the economic struggles of voters have boosted Democrats. But with less than a month to go, there is no complacency For once, Democrats and Donald Trump might be in agreement: “Pretend I’m on the ticket,” the historically unpopular president has instructed supporters . Midterms are in large part a referendum on the incumbent, and Trump’s war on Iran and its impact on the cost of living have boosted support for Democrats. With less than a month to go, they have reason to be upbeat . The party has a mountain to climb after the devastating defeats of 2024, and the gerrymandering of Republicans, but surveys give it a lead of about nine points on the generic ballot, which measures preference for parties rather than specific candidates. Attention has turned from the prospects of seizing the House, where Democrats are forecast a clear majority, to what once seemed like the highly optimistic possibility of taking the Senate too. items.summary: De VN-organisatie voor migratie en hulp aan vluchtelingen (IOM) slaat alarm over de situatie in Jemen. Sinds het weer oplaaien van de strijd tussen de Houthi's en het regeringsleger, begin vorige maand , zijn zo'n 200.000 Jemenieten op de vlucht geslagen. "Mensen rennen voor hun leven maar vinden nergens veiligheid", zegt IOM-directeur Amy Pope. "Ze hebben nu onderdak, eten en veiligheid nodig. Onze mensen zijn ter plekke, maar de financiering niet." Pope vraagt donorlanden om in actie te komen. "Jemen mag geen vergeten crisis worden. De wereld heeft de middelen om te helpen. Die moeten nu gebruikt worden." Ruin dertien jaar Voor veel vluchtelingen is het niet de eerste keer dat ze hun woonplek moeten verlaten. De burgeroorlog in Jemen duurt al ruim dertien jaar. Die begon met een opstand van de door Iran gesteunde Houthi's. Het regeringsleger heeft de steun van Saudi-Arabië. Door bemiddeling van de VN kwam in 2022 een staakt-het-vuren tot stand. items.summary: The author of Moneyball brings his exceptional narrative skills to bear on Musk’s anti-government crusade Donald Trump’s catastrophic errors get so much attention that his systemic ones can easily be missed. While the world looks on in dismay at his farcical war in Iran, the thuggery of Ice agents or clownish attacks on erstwhile allies like Canada and Denmark, the core functions of the American government are slowly disintegrating. It is harder to get people to focus on the machinery of the state because the effects are often slow and hard to pin down. Outbreaks of disease – such as the recent wave of explosive diarrhoea across the US – might have happened anyway, but were probably made worse by lay-offs at the Centers for Disease Control. Likewise, Trump is not directly responsible for natural disasters, but response times in the past year may have been hampered by mass redundancies at the National Weather Service. Cuts to tax collection also seem to have reduced revenue by multiple billions, though we cannot be sure of the causal relationship. Continue reading...

clusters.headline: Nieuwe verdachte aangehouden in Londen voor voorbereiden aanslag bij luchtmachtbasis

items.title: Nieuwe verdachte aangehouden in Londen voor voorbereiden aanslag bij luchtmachtbasis
items.summary: In Londen is een nieuwe verdachte aangehouden op verdenking van het voorbereiden van een terroristische aanslag bij de luchtmachtbasis in Fairford. Dat meldt de contraterrorisme-afdeling van de Britse politie. Het gaat om een 22-jarige man met de Britse nationaliteit. In hetzelfde gebied is ook een woning doorzocht. Op 27 september werd alarm geslagen bij een Britse luchtmachtbasis in het graafschap Gloucestershire, nadat er verdachte witte bestelbusjes waren gespot. De politie vreesde dat er explosieven in de witte busjes lagen en woningen werden uit voorzorg ontruimd. Er werden enkel blikken benzine in de busjes gevonden. The joint statement was released by the US and endorsed by Argentina, Canada, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Guyana, Paraguay, Peru, and Trinidad and Tobago. "On 5 October, the undersigned nations, condemn the terrorist actions and other malign influence operations in our hemisphere by Iran and its terrorist proxies," it read. "These hostile efforts include a range of Iranian and proxy-sponsored lethal plotting, illicit fundraising, political interference and foreign influence activities, and operations meant to bolster terrorist networks, coerce perceived enemies, compromise legal or administrative processes, and harm regional security." The joint statement indicated that the countries "stand united" against "such threats", demanding that Tehran and "its proxies must halt these actions now".

Gulf states such as Qatar, the UAE, Bahrain, and Kuwait faced thousands of missile and drone strikes launched by Iran in retaliation for the US-Israeli attack on the Islamic Republic on 28 February. More recently, Saudi Arabia has come under attack from the Houthis in Yemen. The Houthis and Iran targeted civilian infrastructure like pipelines, energy facilities and, in one case, a nuclear energy plant. Reuters' assessment is likely to cast new doubt on how Gulf states describe strikes on their territories. For example, Saudi Arabia’s energy ministry said that a Houthi drone strike caused a "limited fire" at the headquarters of the kingdom's national oil company, Aramco, in Dhahran. items.title: Delegations from over ten countries walk out of Israeli president's CICA summit speech
items.summary: Delegations from over ten countries walk out of Israeli president's CICA summit speech Representatives from more than 10 countries, including Turkey, walked out of the Conference on Interaction and Confidence Building Measures in Asia (CICA) summit in Azerbaijan as Israeli President Isaac Herzog began his speech on Thursday. Iran’s deputy legal affairs minister called for Israel to be expelled from CICA following Herzog's speech in Baku. Kazem Gharibabadi was quoted as saying by Iran's IRIB news that “sustainable security” in Asia was not achieved through “threats and pressure, but through mutual respect, trust-building and equal cooperation among independent states”. “If the international community does not stop America and Israel today, their aggression will spread to all independent countries. The most important source of insecurity and instability in Asia, especially in West Asia, is the Zionist (Israeli) regime; it is time for this regime to be expelled from the CICA mechanism,” he warned.

items.title: Chinese refiners rush to buy Middle East crude as stocks fall, Kpler says
items.summary: Chinese refiners rush to buy Middle East crude as stocks fall, Kpler says Chinese refiners are stepping up purchases of Middle Eastern crude as record inventory drawdowns and a recovery in refinery activity boost demand for prompt cargoes, according to analytics firm Kpler. Chinese buyers have secured at least 80 million barrels of Saudi crude since mid-September, Kpler said on X. China’s onshore crude inventories fell by about 1.6 million barrels per day in September, the fastest pace on record. Refinery throughput is projected to reach 14.2 million barrels per day by December, adding to pressure on refiners to rebuild stocks. At the same time, Chinese refiners need to replace roughly 1 million barrels per day of Iranian supply, with the US blockade still in place, according to Kpler. Stronger Chinese demand could limit further weakness in Dubai crude pricing, particularly as escalating regional tensions continue to threaten supply flows.

items.title: Pakistan president urges Iran, US to honour Islamabad MoU
items.summary: Pakistan president urges Iran, US to honour Islamabad MoU Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari has urged the US and Iran to exercise restraint and honour their commitments under the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding. The MoU is a 14-point interim peace agreement signed electronically on 17-18 June between the United States and Iran, with Pakistan acting as the primary mediator. Zardari called for differences to be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy, emphasising the importance of safe maritime navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, according to a statement from his office. His remarks came during a meeting with Russian Interior Minister Vladimir Kolokoltsev in Islamabad. Zardari warned that the conflict posed serious challenges to regional stability, global energy security, trade and supply chains, stressing the need to respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of all states. Kolokoltsev is on a four-day official visit to Pakistan, the first by a Russian interior minister to the South Asian country.

items.title: Attacks on Hormuz shipping at wartime high, report says
items.summary: Attacks on Hormuz shipping at wartime high, report says Iranian missile and drone attacks on ships in and around the Strait of Hormuz were at their most intense in the two weeks to 11 October, the highest level since the US-Israeli strikes began seven months ago, the Financial Times reported. The next most intense period of attacks was during the first two weeks of March, when 13 ships were hit, the newspaper said, citing data from naval agency UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), which monitors marine security in the region. Shipowners are reconsider carrying cargoes in the region, the report said. Six vessels were attacked on Sunday alone, making it the deadliest day of attacks on shipping near the strait since the start of the conflict, FT calculated. It added that oil shipments through Hormuz fell to just 2.9 million barrels on 11 October, the lowest daily volume this month, according to Kpler.

items.title: Iranian nuclear technology safe from US attacks, says atomic energy chief
items.summary: Iranian nuclear technology safe from US attacks, says atomic energy chief The head of Iran's atomic energy agency said on Sunday that the country's nuclear technology is safe from external disruption and cannot be halted by threats, pressure or attacks. Mohammad Eslami, the chief of the Atomic Energy Organisation of Iran (AEOI), said Iran's nuclear advances are a national achievement and were a testament to the dedication of Iranian scientists. “Overt threats by US officials to use tactical weapons against Iran’s nuclear facilities - delivered right from the United Nations podium - and talk of destroying Iran’s ancient civilisation, reveal helplessness in the face of a pioneering nation that has historically been the cradle of science, knowledge and technology,” Eslami was quoted as saying by Iran’s semi-official Tasnim news agency, adding that the nation will not surrender to excessive demands. US President Donald Trump has repeatedly affirmed Washington's intention to wipe out Iran's nuclear capabilities and ensure that the country will never be able to develop the technology.

items.title: Increased vessel attacks drive Hormuz oil exports 'sharply lower', report says
items.summary: Increased vessel attacks drive Hormuz oil exports 'sharply lower', report says Hormuz oil exports were “sharply lower,” falling to a seven-day average of 9.9 million barrels per day as of October 7, 42 percent below prewar levels and down from about 15.5 million in September, according to Kpler data cited by the Financial Times. Kpler said that flows had recovered to prewar levels in September but "intensified attacks on vessels" had driven exports "sharply lower" this week. Energy analyst Rory Johnston also said that the latest estimate puts Hormuz seven-day average oil flow peaking at 16.2 mbpd on September 24. "Then Iran really picked up its shipping attacks and that flow unsurprisingly pulled back by 3-4 mbpd," he wrote on X. "Now seeing flow at 12-13 mbpd over the past two weeks."

items.title: Oil prices ease after Trump rules out Iran attack before midterms
items.summary: Oil prices ease after Trump rules out Iran attack before midterms Oil prices eased slightly on Thursday after US President Donald Trump ruled out attacking Iran before next month's midterm elections, saying Washington was holding "productive discussions" with Tehran. Prices had soared earlier in the day following reports that the US could launch fresh strikes on Iran before the vote, raising fears of further supply disruptions. Republicans are fighting to keep control of both houses of Congress in the midterms, while US diesel prices are at record highs.

items.title: Not since 9/11 has the UK faced such a security crisis – and threat to our liberal principles | Gaby Hinsliff
items.summary: The combination of Iranian, Russian and Chinese aggression is deeply worrying: just how much more concerned about security should the country be? The first time the window-rattling roar of a B-1 bomber woke me up this summer, I thought for one crazed second we were under attack. By the second time, I’d learned to recognise the sound of US planes taking off from their base at RAF Fairford for what it was: a reminder that although Britain wants no part in this war with Iran, we cannot quite escape the consequences. We’ll feel them at the petrol pump , or in the supermarket this autumn, or in this winter’s heating bills . But living under the flight path adds an extra edge to it. The skies finally fell silent last week, but only because the bombers have been hastily summoned home after an alleged terrorist plot to attack Fairford, in which (according to the prime minister) there are “ strong indications that Iran played a part ”. items.title: Is Iran poised to withdraw from the Non-Proliferation Treaty?
items.summary: In September, as the media focused its attention on the conflict in the Strait of Hormuz and the debates at the U.N. General Assembly, some internal developments in Iran went all but unnoticed. On September 28, 32 Iranian conservatives published an open letter calling for Iran to withdraw from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) as a matter of urgency. Since the “ snapback ” of U.N. sanctions on Iran in September 2025, ultraconservative Iranian lawmakers have regularly pushed for pulling out of the NPT, under which the vast majority of states have committed to not develop nuclear weapons. The Majles — Iran’s parliament — drafted a law that would have initiated the move in 2025, but it has yet to move forward. In September, some lawmakers submitted new “triple-urgency” legislation to the Majles ’ president, Mohammad Baqer Ghalibaf, who is also currently Iran’s chief negotiator These continuous calls by ultraconservatives to withdraw from the NPT have yet to produce an actual withdrawal because of a lack of political consensus. items.title: Will Americans ever escape this 'imperialist realism'?
items.summary: Last week, after nearly two decades of fighting, the U.S. finally pulled the plug on its seemingly endless war in Iraq. Like our exit from Afghanistan just a few years ago, the end of fighting in Iraq was met with an eerie quiet. It doesn’t take much to figure out why so little attention is paid to the end of these wars: they mark yet another loss for America and the people in Washington who insist our military power can solve every problem, everywhere. Both conflicts are examples of American hubris — strategically incoherent wars fought with American lives at the expense of too many Iraqis and Afghans lives. But, of course, we refuse to learn our lesson. The week before Americans finally vacated Iraq, President Donald Trump took to his proverbial pulpit at the U.N. to brag about his exploitation of Venezuela for oil, declaring “to the victor goes the spoils.” It was a stark expression of how America’s domination of the global order — it’s imperialism, if you will — really works. items.title: The Geoeconomic Implications of the Iran War: An Early Examination
items.summary: The Geoeconomic Implications of the Iran War: An Early Examination Antoine Thu, 10/08/2026 - 02:00 Strategic Security Analyses Global Key points Globalisation has rested on a set of functions long treated as background conditions: transit through maritime choke points, insurability, dollar settlement, critical material inputs and protection by a hegemonic power. In practice, each is an excludable asset held by an identifiable actor, and the Iran war has demonstrated that they can be withheld and monetised. The war followed the failure of the most ambitious campaign of economic coercion yet attempted. In this campaign, sanctions functioned as an antechamber to military action rather than as its substitute, and the resort to a naval blockade to halt Iranian oil exports amounted to an admission that the financial coercion strategy had failed. Iran’s monetisation of the Strait of Hormuz followed a path already opened by US tariffs and export controls, and by Chinese restrictions on critical materials. The Iran-aligned Houthis took responsibility earlier for a flurry of attacks that included firing a ballistic missile at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, as the conflict deepens with Saudi Arabia, which backs Yemen's government. "On Tuesday and Wednesday... An Egyptian and an Algerian national were killed at Abha airport, and a Sudanese national was killed at the airport in Riyadh, the agency said, with 36 people wounded in the attacks.

items.title: The Guardian view on the US midterms: the cost of living is on the ballot, but this is about democracy too | Editorial
items.summary: Donald Trump’s unpopularity and the economic struggles of voters have boosted Democrats. But with less than a month to go, there is no complacency For once, Democrats and Donald Trump might be in agreement: “Pretend I’m on the ticket,” the historically unpopular president has instructed supporters . Midterms are in large part a referendum on the incumbent, and Trump’s war on Iran and its impact on the cost of living have boosted support for Democrats. With less than a month to go, they have reason to be upbeat . The party has a mountain to climb after the devastating defeats of 2024, and the gerrymandering of Republicans, but surveys give it a lead of about nine points on the generic ballot, which measures preference for parties rather than specific candidates. Attention has turned from the prospects of seizing the House, where Democrats are forecast a clear majority, to what once seemed like the highly optimistic possibility of taking the Senate too. items.summary: The author of Moneyball brings his exceptional narrative skills to bear on Musk’s anti-government crusade Donald Trump’s catastrophic errors get so much attention that his systemic ones can easily be missed. While the world looks on in dismay at his farcical war in Iran, the thuggery of Ice agents or clownish attacks on erstwhile allies like Canada and Denmark, the core functions of the American government are slowly disintegrating. It is harder to get people to focus on the machinery of the state because the effects are often slow and hard to pin down. Outbreaks of disease – such as the recent wave of explosive diarrhoea across the US – might have happened anyway, but were probably made worse by lay-offs at the Centers for Disease Control. Likewise, Trump is not directly responsible for natural disasters, but response times in the past year may have been hampered by mass redundancies at the National Weather Service. items.title: Iran Faces Severe Challenges to Rebuild Missile and Drone Production
items.summary: With the significant Israeli and U.S. military attacks against Iran in 2025 and early 2026, analysts have discussed and debated Iran’s ability to replenish its missile and drone arsenal. Since 2024, Iran has burned through thousands of ballistic missiles, cruise missiles, and one-way attack drones in its retaliatory attacks against Israel, U.S. military bases, and other targets in the region. In addition, air and missile strikes destroyed many more Iranian missiles and drones along with their launchers. items.title: US and several allies say Iran committed 'terrorist actions'
items.summary: US and several allies say Iran committed 'terrorist actions' The US and nine other countries across the Americas in a joint statement condemned what they called Iran's "terrorist actions". The joint statement was released by the US and endorsed by Argentina, Canada, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominican Republic, Guyana, Paraguay, Peru, and Trinidad and Tobago. "On 5 October, the undersigned nations, condemn the terrorist actions and other malign influence operations in our hemisphere by Iran and its terrorist proxies," it read. "These hostile efforts include a range of Iranian and proxy-sponsored lethal plotting, illicit fundraising, political interference and foreign influence activities, and operations meant to bolster terrorist networks, coerce perceived enemies, compromise legal or administrative processes, and harm regional security." The joint statement indicated that the countries "stand united" against "such threats", demanding that Tehran and "its proxies must halt these actions now".
